text:
Emma: Huge shoutout to Raj for single-handedly saving today’s all-hands when the A/V died. :raised_hands: You are a legend.
Priya: Story time pls — what happened?
Raj: HDMI feed from the docking station fried during the intro. I swapped inputs, reseated cables, and rerouted the laptop through the backup switch. Mic gain was funky so I tuned levels too. We hit live at +6 minutes. :sunglasses:
Ben: That was surgical. Walked into the room and thought 'what chaos' and then Raj was like 'I got this'. Instant calm. :100:
Emma: Recorded the moment everyone clapped when the slides re-appeared. Will add to the highlights reel.
People-Ops: Can we get Raj a team lunch voucher and a "AV Savior" badge? Also adding to monthly kudos email.
Raj: No need, but thank you! If anyone wants a quick how-to for the backup pipeline I can do a 10-min runthrough next week.
Priya: Yes please. Also, @Facilities can we label the backup switch and the spare HDMI kit so future panics are faster?
Facilities: Noted. We'll add labels and tape a quick 1-page cheat sheet inside the AV cabinet.
AV-Bot: Event log: 2025-11-18T15:02:37Z - HDMI handshake failure; 15:08:12Z - backup switch activated manually; 15:08:42Z - mic gain adjusted. Tagged technician: Raj. :wrench:
Ben: Tiny bit of constructive feedback: maybe a 'handoff' protocol so someone otherwise occupied knows to redirect people away from stage while we fix things.
Emma: Agree. Raj, if you run the 10-min walkthrough, we’ll add the protocol to the runbook and do a 1-page laminated checklist.
Raj: Cool, I'll draft it and drop it in the #eng-ops channel. No one should ever fear a dead HDMI again. :grin:
Priya: Coffee and pastry for Raj this afternoon? My treat.
Raj: I will accept caffeination and gratitude. Thanks everyone!
Emma: Official applause emoji cascade. :clap: :clap: :clap:
